chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Saeed, from Zakariyya ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Amr, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Allah swore upon Himself that he shall not sit upon the cushions of Paradise the one who allows others into his behind. So I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'So-and-so is intellectual and understanding, inviting people unto himself. Allah has afflicted him.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Does he do that in the congregational mosque?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'So, does he do it upon the door of his house?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'So where does he do it?' I said: 'When he is alone.' He said: 'So Allah has not afflicted him. This one is doing it for pleasure. He shall not sit upon the cushions of Paradise.'

key_terms.يُؤْتَى فِي دُبُرِهِ: Allows others into his behind (anal intercourse)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between public and private anal intercourse in Shia jurisprudence regarding exclusion from Paradise?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between anal intercourse performed for public display or social status versus private pleasure, noting that the former is a greater affliction. The scholar notes that doing it in the mosque or one's door signifies a desire for public recognition, whereas doing it when alone is merely for personal gratification, thus sparing one from the specific exclusion from the 'cushions of Paradise' (namāqir al-jannah). This highlights the Shia emphasis on the intention and context of bodily acts in determining spiritual consequence.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Saeed, from Zakariyya Bin Muhammad, from his father, from Amro, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Sword upon Himself<sup>asws</sup> that he shall not sit upon the cushions of the Paradise, the one who allows others into his behind’.

So I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘So and so intellectual, one of understanding, is inviting people unto himself. Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Afflicted him’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Does he do that in the Masjid gathering?’ I said, ‘No’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So, does he do it upon the door of his house?’ I said, ‘No’. He<sup>asws</sup> said:’ So where does he do it?’ I said, ‘When he is alone’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has not Afflicted him. This one is doing it for pleasure. He shall not sit upon the cushions of the Paradise’.
en.sarwar: 8. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from Muhammad ibn Sa‘id from Zakariya ibn Muhammad from his father from ‘Amr who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘I swear upon myself that one who allows sexual intercourse in his anus will not be allowed to sit on the fine furnishings of paradise.’

I then said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, that so and so is a man of reason and deep understanding, calls people to himself and Allah has made him to suffer from this sickness. He (the Imam) asked, ‘Does he do it in the central Masjid?’ I replied, ‘No, he does not do it in the central Masjid.’ He (the Imam) asked, ‘Does he do it at the door of his house?’ I replied, ‘No, he does not do it there.’ He (the Imam) asked, ‘Where does he do it.’ I replied, ‘When he is in private.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Allah then has not caused him to suffer from the sickness, he enjoys it and he will not be allowed to sit on the fine furnishings of paradise.’”
